newsitem.title: JORDAN: Jordan stocks end weekly trade down 0.4 percent.
newsitem.headline: Jordan stocks end weekly trade down 0.4 percent.

text.p: Jordanian shares fell for a fourth consecutive day in shallow trading on Wednesday, ending the week just 0.4 percent down from last week's close.
The Amman Financial Market 60-share index fell 0.24 points to 148.12 points in turnover worth 648,000 dinars ($915,000), most of it in block deals.

"Turnover is still very weak, but there's not much of a (price) drop," one trader said. The index has fallen daily since Saturday's close of 148.75 points, but the slide was gradual and brokers say the market remains in wait-and-see mode.
Arab Bank Group ARBG.AM, which is expected to issue a bonus share issue soon, dominated trade once again and accounted for 45 percent of the day's turnover before closing unchanged at 247 dinars.
"There was one buyer chasing the stock because of the bonus share," said one broker. "There were plenty of people happy to use the chance to sell off their stocks."

Union Bank Savings Investment rose 0.07 dinars to 1.52 dinars. Shares worth 55,000 dinars were traded but brokers said there were just five transactions and there was little interest from the floor in the stock.
Jordan Expatriate Investment also rose 0.05 dinars to one dinar in turnover of 175,000 dinars dominated by large block transactions.
The rise helped push up service sector stocks but industrial stocks, most affected by the continued pessimism over continued sanctions on Iraq, fell back 0.45 percent.
"If you take away the private contracts, there was only about 130,000 dinars of trade on the whole market today," a broker said.
Overall nine shares rose, 10 fell and 16 traded but closed unchanged.
